grammarRules.title: Capitalize the pronoun I
grammarRules.explanation: The subject pronoun I is always capitalized.
grammarRules.explanationEs: El pronombre I siempre se escribe con mayúscula.

grammarRules.title: Spell teacher correctly
grammarRules.explanation: The word is spelled teacher.
grammarRules.explanationEs: La palabra se escribe teacher.

grammarRules.title: Use an article before a singular job
grammarRules.titleEs: Usa un artículo antes de una profesión singular
grammarRules.explanation: Use a/an before a singular countable job noun.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa a/an antes de un sustantivo contable singular que indique una profesión.

grammarRules.title: Choose a or an by sound
grammarRules.titleEs: Elige a o an según el sonido
grammarRules.explanation: Use an before a vowel sound, and a before a consonant sound.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa an antes de un sonido vocálico y a antes de un sonido consonántico.

grammarRules.title: Match be to the subject
grammarRules.explanation: Use am with I, is with he/she/it, and are with you/we/they.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa am con I, is con he/she/it y are con you/we/they.

grammarRules.title: Use the base verb with plural subjects
grammarRules.titleEs: Usa el verbo base con sujetos plurales
grammarRules.explanation: In the present simple, plural subjects use the base verb form.
grammarRules.explanationEs: En presente simple, los sujetos plurales usan la forma base del verbo.

grammarRules.title: Add -s/-es with he, she or it
grammarRules.titleEs: Añade -s/-es con he, she o it
grammarRules.explanation: In affirmative present simple, he/she/it usually takes a verb ending in -s or -es.
grammarRules.explanationEs: En presente simple afirmativo, he/she/it normalmente requiere un verbo terminado en -s o -es.

grammarRules.title: Use -ing after enjoy
grammarRules.explanation: Enjoy is followed by a noun or a verb ending in -ing.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Después de enjoy se usa un sustantivo o un verbo terminado en -ing.

grammarRules.title: Use common patterns after like
grammarRules.titleEs: Usa patrones frecuentes después de like
grammarRules.explanation: Like can be followed by a noun, a verb ending in -ing, or to + base verb.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Like puede ir seguido de un sustantivo, un verbo con -ing o to + verbo base.

grammarRules.title: Put adjectives before nouns
grammarRules.titleEs: Coloca los adjetivos antes del sustantivo
grammarRules.explanation: In a typical English noun phrase, an adjective comes before the noun.
grammarRules.explanationEs: En una frase nominal típica en inglés, el adjetivo va antes del sustantivo.

grammarRules.title: Avoid accidental repeated connectors
grammarRules.explanation: Do not repeat the same connector twice in a row unless quoting or deliberately repeating it.
grammarRules.explanationEs: No repitas el mismo conector dos veces seguidas, salvo que estés citando o repitiendo deliberadamente.
examples: I teach robotics and I enjoy it.
incorrect: I teach and and enjoy it.

grammarRules.title: Handle words not in the vocabulary list
grammarRules.titleEs: Gestiona palabras que no están en la lista
grammarRules.explanation: An unknown word is not automatically an error. Use context and grammar; suggest spelling only when the match is strong and unambiguous.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Una palabra desconocida no es automáticamente un error. Usa el contexto y la gramática; sugiere ortografía solo cuando la coincidencia sea clara y no ambigua.

grammarRules.title: Join compound job titles with and
grammarRules.explanation: Use and to join the two fields in this compound job title.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa and para unir las dos áreas de esta profesión compuesta.
examples: I am a technology and robotics teacher.
incorrect: I am a technology an robotics teacher.

grammarRules.title: Present Continuous
grammarRules.explanation: Use be + verb-ing for actions happening now.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa be + verbo terminado en -ing para acciones que ocurren ahora.
examples: The students are building a robot.

grammarRules.title: Past Simple for finished events
grammarRules.explanation: Use the past form for completed past events, often with a finished time expression.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa la forma pasada para hechos terminados, a menudo con una expresión de tiempo pasado.
examples: We built a robot last week.

grammarRules.title: Going to for plans
grammarRules.explanation: Use be going to + base verb for intentions and plans.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa be going to + verbo base para intenciones y planes.
examples: I am going to build a robot.
We are going to study English.
incorrect: I going to build a robot.

grammarRules.title: There is / There are
grammarRules.explanation: Use there is with a singular noun and there are with a plural noun.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa there is con un sustantivo singular y there are con uno plural.
examples: There is a robot in the lab.
incorrect: There are a robot in the lab.

grammarRules.title: Basic question word order
grammarRules.explanation: In many present-simple questions, use do/does + subject + base verb.
grammarRules.explanationEs: En muchas preguntas en presente simple, usa do/does + sujeto + verbo base.

grammarRules.title: Can and can't for ability
grammarRules.titleEs: Can y can't para expresar capacidad
grammarRules.explanation: Use can/can't + base verb to express ability or inability.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa can/can't + verbo base para expresar capacidad o incapacidad.
incorrect: I can to explain the project.

grammarRules.title: Comparatives
grammarRules.explanation: Use comparative forms to compare two people or things.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa formas comparativas para comparar dos personas o cosas.
examples: This robot is faster than that one.
English is more useful for this project.

grammarRules.title: Much and many
grammarRules.explanation: Use many with countable plural nouns and much with uncountable nouns.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa many con sustantivos contables en plural y much con incontables.

grammarRules.title: Prepositions of time
grammarRules.explanation: Use at for clock times, on for days and dates, and in for months, years and longer periods.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa at para horas, on para días y fechas, e in para meses, años y periodos largos.

grammarRules.title: Present Perfect for experiences
grammarRules.explanation: Use have/has + past participle to talk about experiences without specifying a finished past time.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa have/has + participio para hablar de experiencias sin indicar un momento pasado terminado.

grammarRules.title: Present Perfect vs Past Simple
grammarRules.titleEs: Presente perfecto frente a pasado simple
grammarRules.explanation: Use Past Simple with a finished past time; use Present Perfect for experience or a period connected to now.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa pasado simple con un tiempo pasado terminado y presente perfecto para experiencias o periodos conectados con el presente.
examples: I have visited Bogotá several times.

grammarRules.title: Modals for advice
grammarRules.explanation: Use should + base verb to give advice.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa should + verbo base para dar consejos.

grammarRules.title: Connectors for contrast and concession
grammarRules.explanation: Use although to introduce a contrasting clause; use however to connect contrasting statements.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa although para introducir una oración de contraste y however para conectar afirmaciones contrastantes.
examples: Although it was difficult, we finished.
It was difficult. However, we finished.
incorrect: Although it was difficult, but we finished.

grammarRules.title: First Conditional
grammarRules.explanation: Use if + present simple, will + base verb for a real future possibility.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa if + presente simple, will + verbo base para una posibilidad futura real.
examples: If we practise, we will improve.
incorrect: If we will practise, we will improve.

grammarRules.title: Defining relative clauses
grammarRules.explanation: Use who for people and which/that for things in common defining relative clauses.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa who para personas y which/that para cosas en oraciones relativas especificativas comunes.
examples: The teacher who helped me was patient.
The robot that we built works.
incorrect: The teacher which helped me was patient.

grammarRules.title: Basic passive voice
grammarRules.explanation: Use be + past participle when the action or result is more important than the agent.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa be + participio cuando la acción o el resultado importa más que quién la realiza.
examples: The robot was designed by students.
The project is tested every week.
incorrect: The robot was design by students.

grammarRules.title: Sequence connectors
grammarRules.explanation: Use first, then, after that and finally to make a process or story easier to follow.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa first, then, after that y finally para organizar un proceso o relato.
examples: First, connect the sensor. Then, upload the code.
incorrect: First connect the sensor finally upload the code.
